nl:
A multiplayer game lobby uses a matchmaker that circulates a single write token around a ring of players so that only one player may edit the shared lobby roster at any moment. The shared roster is represented by a running record value plus a version counter; each committed edit adds that player's own contribution to the record and bumps the version by one. A player may only stage and commit an edit while it currently holds the token; when it releases, the token advances to the next seat in the ring. Because the token serializes writers, an edit read-modify-writes the record without another writer interleaving, so no player's contribution can be silently overwritten by a concurrent writer. A privileged admin may seize the token from whoever holds it at any time, but the admin's seizure does not itself edit the record, it only reassigns who may write next. The record therefore always equals the sum of every contribution that has been committed so far.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared record value always equals the total of all player contributions that have been committed, so no committed update is ever lost.
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Players = {p1, p2, p3}
  Delta = 1
  MaxVer = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates

nl:
An airport baggage router controls conveyor belts that are grouped into zones. Two independent router instances, A and B, share one common pool of zones and belts. To service a belt, a router must first take the coarse lock on the belt's parent zone, and only then may it take the fine lock on the individual belt: this is hierarchical two-level locking. A zone lock may be held by at most one router at a time, and likewise a belt lock. A router progresses through phases: idle, then holding a zone (coarse), then holding a belt within that zone (fine). When it finishes it releases the belt, then the zone. A global counter records how many bags have been routed, one per belt release. The essential correctness condition is that a router may only hold a belt while it also holds that belt's parent zone, so a fine lock is never held without its covering coarse lock.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a belt lock is held by a router, that same router also holds the coarse lock on the belt's parent zone.

INVARIANT FineImpliesCoarse

nl:
A print shop spooler coordinates workers that print jobs on printers, where each printer contains several trays. Locking is hierarchical: a worker must first be granted ownership of a printer (the coarse resource) and only then may it seize one of that printer's trays (the fine resource) to print. Each printer carries an epoch number; when the spooler revokes a printer from its current owner it advances that printer's epoch and clears any tray the owner held, so a worker that was merely slow (never failed) but has fallen behind now carries a stale epoch. A worker records the epoch it believed current when granted. A worker may print on a tray only while it owns the tray's parent printer and its recorded epoch still equals the printer's current epoch. This prevents a stale or unauthorized worker, one whose grant has been superseded, from ever completing a print. A global counter tallies completed prints.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Any worker that holds a tray also owns that tray's parent printer with a recorded epoch equal to the printer's current epoch, so no stale or unauthorized worker holds a tray.

nl:
A smart-home door-lock network processes unlock requests using optimistic concurrency control with retry. There is a shared authoritative version number. Each controller node, when it wants to apply an unlock request, first optimistically reads the current version into a private snapshot together with the request it intends to apply. To commit, the node performs a compare-and-set: it may finalize the unlock only if the version it snapshotted still equals the live version and the request has not already been applied. A successful commit physically opens that door (an irreversible action), advances the shared version by one, and clears the node's snapshot. If a node finds its snapshot version no longer matches the live version, it discards the snapshot and retries. If it notices its target request was already opened by someone else, it aborts. A controller may be slow but never crashes, so a lagging node can still be holding an old snapshot. Because a commit advances the version, any node still holding a snapshot for a request that has since been opened must be holding a version strictly older than the live one, so its stale compare-and-set can never succeed and no door is opened twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Any node whose held snapshot targets a request whose door is already open must have snapshotted a version strictly older than the live version, so a stale request can never be committed a second time.

An air-traffic control system allocates a single shared runway to flights. A pool of controllers runs a leader-election protocol with failover: at any time at most one live controller is the elected leader, and only the leader may grant the runway. A controller may crash silently (without announcing it); to keep the tower operational at most one controller is down at a time, and a downed controller can later recover. When the current leader is not alive, any alive controller may take over as the new leader. Each flight moves through phases: idle, waiting for the runway, on the runway (the critical section), and done, after which it may reset to idle. The runway itself is a lock with a single owner. A waiting flight is put on the runway only by a live leader and only when the lock is free, which makes the flight the lock owner; when it leaves, the lock is freed and a landing is tallied. Because the lock has exactly one owner, two flights can never occupy the runway at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A flight is on the runway only while it is the sole owner of the runway lock, so no two flights are ever on the runway simultaneously.

CONSTANTS

  Flights = {f1, f2, f3}
  MaxLanded = 3
INIT Init

INVARIANT RunwayMutex

nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker maintains a single shared stock count of units on hand. Technicians modify the stock with a hierarchical two-level lock: a technician must first take the coarse bank lock, then the fine stock lock, before it may read and write the stock. To perform an update, the holder of the stock lock first snapshots the current stock into its private register; it later commits by writing back its snapshot adjusted by a fixed delta, then releasing the stock lock. Because only the exclusive stock-lock holder can change the stock, a holder's snapshot stays equal to the live stock for the entire time it holds the lock, so no other update can slip in and be overwritten (no lost update). A privileged supervisor may override the whole protocol at any time: the override forcibly clears every technician's hold, frees both locks, and applies an adjustment itself. Stock is capped at a maximum capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: While a technician holds the stock lock, its snapshotted value always equals the live stock, so no concurrent update to the shared stock is ever lost.
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Techs = {t1, t2}
  Delta = 2
  MaxStock = 6
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SnapshotConsistent

nl:
A car-wash conveyor line releases each washed car to the street only after a two-phase commit across several stations (soap, rinse, dry). For one car at a time, a coordinator runs the protocol. In the voting phase each station casts a vote of yes or no at its own pace; a station may be slow but never fails, so votes trickle in asynchronously. Once votes are in, the coordinator decides: if every station voted yes it decides commit, and if any station voted no it decides abort. Releasing the car onto the street is the single irreversible action, and it may occur only after a commit decision, and only once. After a car is released or its transaction aborted, the line resets to start the next car, bounded by a maximum throughput count. The decision, once made for the current car, drives whether release is permitted.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A car is released only after the coordinator has decided commit with every station having voted yes, and it is released at most once per transaction.
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Stations = {soap, rinse, dry}
  MaxCars = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SafeRelease

nl:
A power-grid load shedder decides shed proposals by quorum voting. There is a fixed set of relay nodes, and each shed proposal must gather votes from a quorum (a majority) of nodes before it can be applied. Votes for a proposal accumulate in a set, so a node voting more than once or votes arriving out of order (messages can be reordered) has no extra effect. When a proposal has collected a quorum of votes, it is applied: the proposal is recorded into the shared shed ledger and the total shed load is increased. Applying is guarded so a proposal is applied at most once. The shared ledger is the authoritative record of which sheds took effect. The correctness requirement is that every applied proposal is faithfully present in the shared ledger and was backed by a genuine quorum, so no applied shed is ever lost from the record and none is applied without sufficient votes.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every proposal marked applied is present in the shared shed ledger and had at least a quorum of votes, so no applied update is lost or unbacked.

nl:
A power-grid load shedder manages a fixed total amount of power distributed across three zones plus a spinning reserve. Power is never created or destroyed; it only moves. The controller runs epoch-numbered reconfiguration: a configuration epoch counter is advanced whenever the grid topology is reconfigured, and each zone is marked active or inactive under the current configuration. Operators issue commands that may arrive reordered, so every command carries the epoch it was issued under and is honored only when its epoch matches the current epoch; commands from a superseded epoch are ignored. The honored commands are: shed one unit from an active zone into the reserve, restore one unit from the reserve back into an active zone, and move one unit directly between two active zones. Reconfiguration flips a zone's active flag and advances the epoch. Across every command and reconfiguration, the sum of all zone loads plus the reserve stays exactly equal to the fixed total.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The sum of the three zone loads plus the reserve always equals the fixed total power, so no power is ever created or destroyed.

nl:
A container-ship crane yard feeds lift jobs through a bounded work queue with backpressure. The queue holds a number of pending jobs up to a capacity that can change at runtime as bays open or close. When the queue is at capacity, no new job may be enqueued (backpressure). Cranes process jobs, but a crane may act only when authorized: the yard controller issues authorization tickets stamped with the current authorization epoch, and a crane holds the epoch it was granted. A crane begins processing a job only while holding a ticket whose epoch equals the controller's current authorization epoch, and doing so removes one job from the queue. When the controller revokes authorization it advances the epoch and immediately stops any crane that was mid-process, returning it to idle, so a crane carrying a stale (superseded) ticket can never be found processing. Cranes finish and return to idle on their own.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Any crane that is currently processing holds a ticket whose epoch equals the controller's current authorization epoch, so no stale or unauthorized crane ever processes a job.
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Cranes = {k1, k2}
  MaxCap = 3
  MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleProcessing

nl:
An airport baggage router assigns bags to carousel slots. Exclusive authority to assign is granted by a single circulating token: only the current token holder may allocate or free slots. The token is passed around a ring of router nodes, and because pass messages can be reordered or delayed, the token may end up at any node, but there is always exactly one holder. Each bag has a status: waiting, placed, or removed. The holder places a waiting bag into a currently free slot, which records the assignment both ways: the slot points to the bag and the bag points to the slot. The holder may later remove a placed bag, freeing its slot; a removed bag can recycle back to waiting. The two-way mapping must stay consistent so that a slot is never allocated to two different bags and a bag is never recorded in two slots.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The slot-to-bag and bag-to-slot mappings are always mutual inverses, so no carousel slot is ever allocated to two different bags at once.

A smart-home door-lock network is served by two independent controller instances, A and B, that share one common pool of doors. Ownership of a door is granted by a time-bounded lease: to act on a door a controller acquires a lease stamped with an expiry equal to the current clock plus a fixed lease length. A shared clock ticks forward up to a horizon. The single irreversible action is unlocking a door, which may happen only while the acting controller holds a lease that has not yet expired (the clock is at or before the lease's expiry), and only once per door. The clock at which a door was unlocked is recorded. Once a door is unlocked no new lease may be taken on it, so its lease expiry is frozen. Expired leases may be released. Because an unlock is permitted only under a live lease, the recorded unlock clock of any unlocked door never exceeds that door's lease expiry.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every unlocked door was unlocked at a clock no later than its lease's expiry, so the irreversible unlock only ever happens once and only under a still-valid lease.
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Owners = {A, B}
  Doors = {d1, d2}
  LeaseLen = 1
  Horizon = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT UnlockUnderLiveLease

nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has a single wash bay that is the critical resource: at most one car may occupy it at a time. Admission to the bay is decided by quorum voting: a fixed set of safety controllers must approve a car before it enters. Each car proceeds through phases: idle, requesting (collecting approvals), in the bay, and done, after which it resets to idle. When a car is requesting, controllers cast approval votes at their own pace; a controller may be slow but never fails, so votes accumulate asynchronously in a set. A requesting car may enter the bay only once it has gathered a quorum of approvals and the bay is currently free; entering makes that car the sole bay owner. When the car leaves, the bay owner is cleared and a wash is tallied. Because the bay has a single owner, no two cars can be in the bay at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A car is in the wash bay only while it is the single owner of the bay, so no two cars ever occupy the bay simultaneously.
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Cars = {x1, x2}
  Controllers = {v1, v2, v3}
  Quorum = 2
  MaxWashed = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BayMutex

nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler coordinates surgical teams over operating rooms grouped by department. Locking is hierarchical: to operate in a room, a team must first hold the coarse lock on the room's department, then the fine lock on the specific room. Each operating room is a critical resource; at most one team may be operating in it. A team advances through phases: idle, holding a department, holding a room within that department, and operating. It records which room it is using. A team may begin operating only while it owns its chosen room and owns that room's department. When finished it releases the room, then the department. A hospital administrator may override the protocol on any room, forcibly preempting whichever team holds it: the override clears that room's lock and returns the preempted team to merely holding its department. Because each room lock has a single owner, two teams can never be operating in the same room at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A team is operating in a room only while it is that room's sole lock owner and also owns the room's department, so no two teams ever operate in the same room simultaneously.
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Teams = {ta, tb}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT RoomMutex

nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser fills prescriptions using optimistic concurrency control with bounded retry. Every prescription carries its own version number and a status of open or filled, and the pharmacy holds a stock of a drug. When a pharmacist wants to fill a prescription it optimistically snapshots that prescription's current version. To fill (the single irreversible dispensing action) it performs a compare-and-set: it may proceed only if its snapshot version still equals the prescription's live version, the prescription is still open, and stock is available. A successful fill marks the prescription filled, advances that prescription's version by one, and decrements stock. If the snapshot no longer matches the live version the pharmacist discards it and retries, up to a retry budget after which it gives up. A pharmacist may be slow but never crashes, so it can hold a stale snapshot. Because a fill advances the prescription's version, any pharmacist still holding a snapshot for a prescription that has since been filled must be holding an outdated version, so its stale compare-and-set can never fill it again.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Any pharmacist whose snapshot targets a prescription that is already filled holds a version different from that prescription's live version, so the irreversible dispense can never happen twice for one prescription.
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Pharmacists = {ph1, ph2}
  Rxs = {rx1, rx2}
  InitStock = 3
  MaxRetry = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleFill

nl:
An airport baggage router allocates carousel slots to bags using two-phase commit across several belt controllers. To allocate a target slot to a bag, a coordinator opens a round naming that bag and slot, then runs a vote: each controller votes yes only if it is alive and sees the target slot as still free, and votes no otherwise. One controller may crash silently at any time; a crashed controller cannot vote yes. The coordinator commits only if every controller voted yes, in which case the slot is bound to the bag in a two-way mapping (slot points to bag, bag points to slot); if any controller voted no or is unavailable, the round aborts. After commit or abort the round resets so another allocation can be attempted. The two-way mapping is kept mutually consistent, so a carousel slot is never bound to two different bags.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The slot-to-bag and bag-to-slot mappings are always mutual inverses, so no carousel slot is ever allocated to two different bags.

A subway signalling system protects track blocks so that no two trains ever occupy the same block. Each block is guarded by a single movement token; entry authority circulates as a token ring, and a train may enter a block only by taking that block's token, which makes the train the block's sole token holder. A train advances through phases per block: approaching, in the block (the critical section), and cleared, after which it may approach again. When a train clears a block it returns the token. Signalling relays that grant the tokens can crash silently; to keep the line moving at most one relay is down at a time, and a downed relay can recover. A grant of a block token to an approaching train requires an alive relay assigned to that block. Because each block token has a single holder, two trains can never be in the same block at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A train is in a block only while it is the sole holder of that block's token, so no two trains ever occupy the same block simultaneously.

A stock exchange opening auction fills a set of price slots in the opening book. The right to fill a given price slot is granted by a time-bounded lease: a market maker acquires a lease on a slot stamped with an expiry equal to the current clock plus a fixed lease length. A shared auction clock ticks forward to a horizon. Lease-request and fill messages can be reordered, so a fill is validated against the live clock rather than assumed in order. A market maker may bind an order to a slot only while holding a lease on that slot that has not expired and while the slot is still unfilled; binding records the slot-to-order and order-to-slot mapping both ways and freezes the lease. Expired leases on unfilled slots may be released and reacquired. Because a slot, once bound, is never rebound, and the two-way mapping is kept mutually consistent, no price slot is ever allocated to two different orders.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The slot-to-order and order-to-slot mappings are always mutual inverses, so no price slot is ever allocated to two different orders.

An airport baggage router allocates carousel slots to bags with two-phase commit across belt agents, and a supervisor may override the protocol. To allocate a target slot to a bag, a coordinator opens a round naming that bag and slot and each agent then casts a yes or no vote; an agent votes yes only if the target slot is currently free. The coordinator commits, binding the slot to the bag in a two-way mapping, only if all agents voted yes and the slot is still free; otherwise it aborts. Independently, a privileged supervisor may force-bind a free slot to a bag directly, bypassing the vote, but only if the slot is free and the bag is unbound, and the supervisor may also force-release an already bound slot, clearing both directions of its mapping. Every binding, whether by commit or by supervisor override, keeps the slot-to-bag and bag-to-slot mappings mutually consistent, so a slot is never bound to two different bags.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The slot-to-bag and bag-to-slot mappings are always mutual inverses, so no carousel slot is ever bound to two different bags.

An airport baggage router allocates carousel slots to bags with two-phase commit across belt agents, and a supervisor may override the protocol. To allocate a target slot to a bag, a coordinator opens a round naming that bag and slot and each agent then casts a yes or no vote; an agent votes yes only if the target slot is currently free. The coordinator commits, binding the slot to the bag in a two-way mapping, only if all agents voted yes and the slot is still free; otherwise it aborts. Independently, a privileged supervisor may force-bind a free slot to a bag directly, bypassing the vote, but only if the slot is free and the bag is unbound, and the supervisor may also force-release an already bound slot, clearing both directions of its mapping. Every binding, whether by commit or by supervisor override, keeps the slot-to-bag and bag-to-slot mappings mutually consistent, so a slot is never bound to two different bags.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The slot-to-bag and bag-to-slot mappings are always mutual inverses, so no carousel slot is ever bound to two different bags.

Two independent power-grid controller instances, A and B, share one pool of shed operations and jointly maintain a shared shed record. Each shed operation is a distinct item in the pool. The system uses epoch-numbered reconfiguration: a configuration epoch is advanced on reconfiguration, and each controller instance carries the epoch it last synced. A controller may apply a shed operation only while its synced epoch equals the current epoch (epoch fencing); applying an operation marks it applied in the instance's local applied set and simultaneously records it into the shared shed record. Reconfiguration advances the epoch, leaving lagging instances fenced out until they resync to the new epoch. The correctness requirement is that the shared record and the set of applied operations never drift apart: every operation that any instance has applied is present in the shared record, and every operation in the shared record has been applied, so no applied shed is ever lost from the record.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of applied shed operations always equals the set recorded in the shared shed record, so no applied update is ever lost from the record.
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Instances = {A, B}
  Ops = {o1, o2, o3}
  MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate

nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm pulls scan tasks from a bounded dispatch queue with backpressure and assigns drones to sectors. The queue holds pending scan tasks up to a fixed capacity; when full, no new task may be enqueued. Each sector is a critical resource that may be actively scanned by at most one drone at a time; a sector is a lock with a single owner. A drone advances through phases: idle, then scanning a sector it has claimed. A drone begins scanning a sector only when the queue has a task to consume and the sector's lock is free, which makes the drone that sector's sole owner and removes one task from the queue. When it finishes it releases the sector lock and returns to idle. A drone may crash silently; to keep coverage going at most one drone is down at a time, and a downed drone is recovered, which also releases any sector it was scanning. Because each sector lock has a single owner, two drones never scan the same sector at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A drone is scanning a sector only while it is the sole owner of that sector's lock, so no two drones ever scan the same sector simultaneously.

CONSTANTS
  Drones = {d1, d2}
  Sectors = {s1, s2}
  Capacity = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SectorMutex

nl:
A library book reservation system tracks a fixed number of copies of a title, each copy always in exactly one of three states: available on the shelf, reserved by a patron, or checked out. Copies are never created or destroyed; a reservation only moves a copy between states. Moving a copy from available to reserved must be approved by quorum voting: a fixed set of branch librarians vote, and a reservation is granted only once a quorum of votes is collected. Librarians may be slow but never fail, so their votes for a pending reservation accumulate asynchronously in a set. Once granted, a copy moves from available to reserved. A reserved copy may then be checked out to the patron, and a checked-out copy may be returned directly to available. Across every reservation, checkout, and return, the counts of available, reserved, and checked-out copies always sum to the fixed total number of copies.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of available, reserved, and checked-out copies always sums to the fixed total number of copies, so no copy is ever created or destroyed.

nl:
A smart-home door-lock network distributes a fixed pool of unlock credits across its lock nodes; credits are never created or destroyed, only moved. Exclusive authority to move credits circulates as a single baton in a token ring: only the current baton holder may transfer credits. The baton holder may hand exactly one credit from its own node to another node (provided its node has a credit to give), and it may pass the baton on to any node. Each node can also be toggled online or offline for maintenance, which does not change any credit counts. A privileged administrator may override the ring at any time to rebalance the network, moving one credit from any node that has one to any other node directly, bypassing the baton. Under every transfer, baton pass, toggle, and administrative rebalance, the total number of credits held across all nodes stays exactly equal to the fixed pool size.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The sum of unlock credits across all nodes always equals the fixed pool size, so no credit is ever created or destroyed.
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Pool = 3
  MaxMoves = 4
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conserved

nl:
A smart-home door-lock network distributes a fixed pool of unlock credits across its lock nodes and a shared vault; credits are never created or destroyed, only moved. Exclusive authority to move credits circulates as a single baton in a token ring: only the current baton holder may transfer credits. The baton holder may hand exactly one credit from its own node to another node (provided its node has a credit to give), and it may deposit one credit from its node into the shared vault or withdraw one credit from the vault back to its node. It may also pass the baton on to any node. Each node can be toggled online or offline for maintenance, which does not change any credit counts. A privileged administrator may override the ring at any time to rebalance the network, moving one credit from any node that has one to any other node directly, bypassing the baton. Under every transfer, deposit, withdrawal, baton pass, toggle, and administrative rebalance, the total number of credits held across all nodes plus the vault stays exactly equal to the fixed pool size.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The sum of unlock credits across all nodes plus the shared vault always equals the fixed pool size, so no credit is ever created or destroyed.
